source.locator: Definition of partial positive and completable graphs in Section 5, Theorem 7 on page 120, and the sequential completion process in Section 7 on pages 122--123
source.verbatim_statement: \(\text{THEOREM 7. }G\text{ is completable if and only if }G\text{ is chordal.}\)

attestation.note: Transcribed from Theorem 7 of the source-of-record PDF; the maximal-clique formulation unfolds the paper's definition of a partial positive matrix, and the constructive clause is located in its Section 7 completion process.

added_lemmas.justification: This is the classical graph-theoretic existence criterion needed to turn coordinatewise partial disturbance covariances into full positive-definite certificates on chordal observation graphs.
added_lemmas.gap: GroneEtAl1984PositiveDefiniteCompletion supplies the matrix-completion substrate; it does not derive the LiMVAM residual criterion, coefficient uniqueness, or the four-cycle observed-moment obstruction proved here.
added_lemmas.consumer: The chordal branch of \(\text{thm:calibration-graph-completion}\) invokes this result after reducing LiMVAM feasibility to one partial covariance matrix per variable.

added_lemmas.justification: This theorem gives the complete population feasibility test for an arbitrary graph of paired views and separates edgewise component alignment from the genuinely global positive-definite completion obstruction.
added_lemmas.gap: The selected-clique certificate in \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\) is automatically completable, while GroneEtAl1984PositiveDefiniteCompletion addresses partial matrices without the LiMVAM residual reduction.  The theorem joins these ingredients and proves that nonchordal calibration graphs require more than positive edge blocks.
added_lemmas.consumer: A partially paired multi-view study can test every candidate order on its actually observed view graph, return coordinatewise max-determinant noise certificates when feasible, and detect nonchordal designs for which local edge checks are insufficient.

proposed_core_edits.name: E_obs

proposed.name: E_obs
proposed.def: The unordered pairs of views whose cross-covariance blocks are observed.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The graph-completion theorem requires an explicit edge set for arbitrary partially paired view designs.

proposed_core_edits.name: G_obs

proposed.name: G_obs
proposed.def: The observed view graph whose vertices are views and whose edges are observed paired cross-view blocks.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The directive requires a theorem for an arbitrary observed view graph, not only a selected clique.

proposed_core_edits.name: O_G

proposed.name: O_G
proposed.def: \(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}\) contains every within-view covariance and exactly the cross-view blocks on \(E_{\mathrm{obs}}\), as defined in \(\text{def:observed-view-graph-moments}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: A distinct observable is needed to state graph-indexed completion without overloading the clique observable \(\mathcal O_S\).

proposed_core_edits.name: Q_pi

proposed.name: Q_pi
proposed.def: \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})\) is the coordinatewise partial disturbance covariance defined in \(\text{def:coordinate-partial-noise-matrix}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The global obstruction is coordinatewise positive-definite completion of a partially specified disturbance covariance.
This definition exposes exactly which covariance blocks are available under a general graph calibration design and states the marginal positivity required by modified Cholesky inversion.
The theorem's second necessary-and-sufficient condition must be a computable partial matrix with explicit specified and unspecified entries.

proposed.citation: R. Grone, C. R. Johnson, E. M. S\'a, and H. Wolkowicz (1984), Positive Definite Completions of Partial Hermitian Matrices, Linear Algebra and its Applications 58, 109--124, doi:10.1016/0024-3795(84)90207-6.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The chordal specialization invokes the classical positive-definite matrix-completion theorem and requires precise source metadata.
